name: Merchant's Arc

stars.name: Arc
stars.notes: Bright F-type star with a wide habitable zone. Its higher luminosity supports habitable conditions at greater orbital distances than typical.

planets.name: Writ
planets.notes: Blasted inner world, tidally locked. Solar collection arrays on the day side power long-range communication relays.

planets.name: Covenant
planets.notes: Primary inhabited world, population 4.1 billion. A temperate planet with vast grassland continents, its cities cluster around ancient spaceport complexes that predate current settlement records.

planets.name: Tithe
planets.notes: Arid but habitable world, population 670 million. Serves as the system's agricultural breadbasket through massive hydroponic arcologies.

planets.name: Bounty
planets.notes: Golden-hued gas giant with a broad ring system. Its largest moon, Purse, hosts a population of 45 million fuel workers and their families.

planets.name: Venture
planets.notes: Enormous outer giant, the system's largest body. Deep atmospheric storms produce exotic compounds harvested by automated skimmer fleets.

planets.name: Annuity
planets.notes: Frozen world with subsurface ocean. Long-term research station studies potential for future colonization.

planets.name: Legacy
planets.notes: Distant ice dwarf at the system's edge. Automated monitoring stations track inbound traffic from deep space.

anomalies.name: The Merchant's Compass
anomalies.notes: A gravitational lens effect that makes the system unusually easy to detect and navigate toward from long range, effectively acting as a natural beacon for approaching vessels.

asteroid_belts.name: The Coffer
asteroid_belts.notes: Primary source of industrial metals and rare earths. Mining operations are tightly regulated by the Arc Commerce Board to maintain stable commodity prices.

stations.name: Arcway Prime
stations.notes: Massive crescent-shaped station that gives the system its name. The curved structure spans 40 kilometers and is visible from Covenant's surface at night.

stations.name: Tithe Gate
stations.notes: Agricultural trade hub specializing in bulk foodstuffs and hydroponic technology. Feeds a dozen neighboring systems.

stations.name: The Purse Annex
stations.notes: Major fuel depot and ship maintenance facility. Long-haul merchants consider it the best repair yard in the corridor.

stations.name: Arc Sentinel
stations.notes: Commerce Board defense station. Screens incoming traffic and provides anti-piracy patrols along the corridor approaches.

faction_control.notes: Elected mercantile parliament representing trade guilds, planetary governments, and independent merchant associations. Known for regulatory stability and fair arbitration.

history: Merchant's Arc was among the earliest systems settled along the Ursine Trade Corridor in 2281, its natural navigational beacon drawing explorers and colonists who recognized its potential as a waypoint.

The construction of Arcway Prime station in 2345, a forty-kilometer crescent that took eighteen years to complete, established Merchant's Arc as the corridor's dominant commercial center and gave the system its modern name.

The Arc Commerce Board was formalized in 2402 after the Trade Guild Wars, replacing the previous patchwork of competing merchant factions with a unified parliamentary system that has maintained stability for over two centuries.
description: Merchant's Arc takes its name from Arcway Prime, the colossal crescent-shaped station that hangs in orbit above Covenant like a silver sickle against the stars. The bright F8V star Arc illuminates seven worlds, two of them inhabited, and the system's position along the Ursine Trade Corridor has made it one of the most important commercial crossroads in its quadrant. Covenant's 4.1 billion inhabitants form the economic engine, while Tithe's hydroponic arcologies feed not only the system but a dozen neighbors, making agricultural exports the second pillar of the Arc economy after transshipment services.

The Arc Commerce Board governs with a reputation for fairness that is the system's most valuable asset. Merchants know that contracts honored in the Arc will be enforced, that arbitration will be impartial, and that the regulatory environment will not shift with political winds. This predictability draws traffic that could route through cheaper but less reliable alternatives, and the system's four stations handle everything from bulk agricultural commodities to luxury goods to military supply contracts. The Merchant's Compass anomaly at the system's edge makes navigation easier for approaching vessels, a natural advantage that early settlers considered almost providential.

The ancient spaceport complexes on Covenant present an enduring mystery. Predating current settlement records by an indeterminate period, their architecture incorporates alloys and construction techniques not consistent with any known human colonial era. The Commerce Board officially classifies them as early-colonial in origin, but independent archaeologists dispute this, pointing to structural elements that appear to predate human interstellar travel by centuries. The Board has restricted access to the deepest excavation sites, citing safety concerns, but critics suspect they fear that the true history of Merchant's Arc might complicate their carefully cultivated narrative of orderly commercial civilization.
